card.architecture: FLUX.1 Fill [dev] 12B rectified-flow DiT, ImagePadForOutpaint canvas extension + native mask conditioning, full-frame sampling + measured color-corrected paste-back
card.summary: Extend an image past its edges with the model trained for outpainting. The canvas is padded on the sides you choose; because the mask is native model conditioning, the border continues the existing scene rather than being a stylistically-similar invention. The border's exposure/tint drift is measured against the untouched pixels and inverted, and the original area is composited back untouched.
card.pick_when: First choice for widening framing or adding head/foot room.

prompt.guidance: Describe the scene being continued, briefly and scene-level ('beautiful scenery', 'a wide city street at dusk'). Anything you name in detail tends to get rendered INTO the new border, so don't re-describe objects that are already in the picture.
prompt.example: a wide city street at dusk, wet pavement, neighbouring shopfronts
prompt.instructions: Natural language. Recommended: 20 steps, euler/normal, CFG 1, guidance ~30. Extend in moderate increments — a very large pad in one pass gives the model little context to continue from.
prompt.negative_guidance: Not supported (CFG 1; the negative is zeroed).

negative.note: Guidance-distilled: real CFG stays 1 and the negative is zeroed out.

speed.measured_note: 12B bf16 cast to fp8_e4m3fn at load, alongside fp16 T5-XXL on 24 GB. Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Drag the frame out on the sides you want to extend, describe the whole enlarged scene, and send.
ui_help.good_for: extending a photo's canvas on any side while keeping the original

edit_use_cases: outpaint: extend the canvas on any side and fill the new border in keeping with the existing scene
